clue.text: East End slang's double Dutch?

parts.note: surface reading: gibberish, talk nobody can follow
setter's reading: in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' is a man's wife, so a double one means two wives at once

explanation.surface: A Londoner's slang sounds like complete gibberish to an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang 'Dutch' (from duchess of Fife, wife) means wife; East End is the traditional Cockney part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Having two wives at the same time is the offence of marrying while already married.

clue.text: You'll need help on clues like this — give in?

indicators.note: in a down clue one word sitting on another is placed above it, so the first piece comes first

parts.note: to back someone is to support or help them
this clue is a down clue

explanation.surface: A beginner admits they need assistance with clues like this one before surrendering.
explanation.walkthrough: The question sounds like a solver's plea for hints; the self-reference is to this being a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To back down is to retreat from a position and yield, a phrasal verb meaning surrender.

clue.text: The Italian will disrupt flying, regular and irregular

indicators.note: to disrupt is to break into the middle of something, so this piece goes inside the other
something flying is moving about freely, so the word after it is scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
il is the Italian masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: An Italian airline passenger is disrupting flights, both scheduled and unscheduled.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters are split open after GUERR and the Italian article goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular is a soldier outside the regular army, which is exactly what a partisan fighter of this kind is.

clue.text: Has to report missing black horse

parts.note: must means has to

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for black is taken away from the preceding word

parts.note: a report is the loud noise of a gun
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Someone must file a report on a missing black horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild or feral horse of the American West.

clue.text: Doddered along, mixed up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: walked slowly, dragging the feet
second meaning: put in random order, like cards

explanation.surface: An old person tottered along, confused.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both walking with dragging feet and jumbling things, as a deck of cards is jumbled before dealing.

clue.text: Trouble with grit one's found in bed

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in trouble
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Trouble arises when grit gets into someone's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber container filled from the kettle is tucked between the sheets to warm them before sleep.

clue.text: Say, bass jammed with piano twice after Love in Vain

indicators.note: a thing jammed with other stuff has it packed inside, so those letters go in the middle

parts.note: a bass is an example of a fish; say signals an example

indicators.note: after tells us the doubled letter follows the one for love in sequence

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, a letter O
P is the musical abbreviation for piano (softly), doubled

explanation.surface: A bassist jams with a pianist after playing the old blues song Love in Vain.
explanation.walkthrough: Love in Vain is a blues song, so the clue sounds musical; the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is excessively concerned with his looks and dress, so dandyish behaviour is conceited.

clue.text: When cycling, quench with lots of water

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the front letter moves round to the back

parts.note: to slake a thirst is to quench it

explanation.surface: A cyclist quenches their thirst with plenty of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Large inland bodies of fresh water collectively hold a great deal of liquid.

clue.text: Grilled, it may cause gluttony — fifth sin a Dantean keeps up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom upwards, backwards
keeps means holds within, so the run of letters is concealed inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of fifth, all of sin and a, and the start of Dantean

explanation.surface: Gluttony is a sin a Dante scholar keeps up, and grilled food may tempt it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dante's Inferno lists the sins, which makes the hidden letters look like literary chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish bacon is a familiar breakfast rasher, and a pastry of the same name tempts overeating.

clue.text: One may buy paints, duty-free oils or mixes

indicators.note: to mix things is to jumble them, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Someone buying paints shops for duty-free oils or ready-mixed colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A home-improvement amateur buys paint and materials to decorate the house without hiring tradespeople.

clue.text: Game with six men we know initially — but one's 11

definitions.text: Game with six men we know initially — but one's 11

parts.note: surface reading: half a dozen people known by their initials
setter's reading: the six kinds of piece are written by initial letters, but the knight's is N, as the word is spoken rather than spelt

explanation.surface: A game played by six familiar men, one of them blunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces are noted K, Q, R, B, N and P; knight gets N because its K is silent, the outspoken (11-across) one.
explanation.definitionFit: This board game of kings, queens, rooks, bishops, knights and pawns uses those six types of piece.

clue.text: Uncivil layabouts poke noses, boxing

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the letters are held inside the words before it

parts.note: letters run from the end of layabouts, through poke, into the start of noses

explanation.surface: Rude idlers poke their noses into things while sparring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blunt says frankly what they think, which can come across as rude or impolite.

clue.text: Walked round — which staff's occupied or inactive?

indicators.note: a place occupied by people has them inside it, so the staff go in the middle
round suggests turning about, so the word before it is read backwards

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, walked
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: Someone walked around asking whose staff were busy and whose were idle.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano or seed lying asleep is temporarily inactive though capable of reviving later.

clue.text: Blackbeard and Calico Jack maybe travel across ocean westwards

indicators.note: in an across clue west is leftwards, so the whole is read from right to left
travelling across an expanse means being spread within it, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an ocean is a sea
to sail is to travel by water

explanation.surface: Two famous pirates sail across the ocean heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackbeard was Edward Teach and Calico Jack was John Rackham, so both names are assumed ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicknames and false names that people go by in place of their real names are examples of assumed identities.

clue.text: Oscar said, Age chooses to regenerate — a fool's errand

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we want the sound of the name rather than its spelling

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Irish writer, whose surname is pronounced like the adjective for untamed

indicators.note: regenerating means forming anew, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde quips that old age chooses to renew itself, which is a futile quest.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeless pursuit of something unattainable is a pointless mission only a fool would undertake.

clue.text: Second group, heavy metal — its purpose is depressing

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a team is a group working together
iron is a dense metal

explanation.surface: A second band plays heavy metal whose whole point is gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Depressing here means pressing down, as on creased clothes, not causing sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: A household appliance pushes down on fabric with heat and vapour to flatten out creases.

clue.text: Strong drink opponents love guzzling squash

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing greedily, so the next word ends up inside the earlier letters

parts.note: East and South are opposing partnerships at bridge
to squash is to press
love is zero, a letter O

explanation.surface: Rivals in love gulp down a fruit squash, a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge East-West oppose North-South, so any E and S pair can be opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A small concentrated coffee made by forcing hot water through ground beans is famously potent.

clue.text: Two French articles aired query into gambling — dirty stuff here?

indicators.note: into means placed within, so the question word is put inside the gambling word

parts.note: la and un are both French articles
washing that has been aired is dry
bets are what gambling involves
to query is to ask

explanation.surface: Two French newspaper pieces raise questions about gambling, the kind of dirt reported in scandal sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: Aired sounds like broadcast, but it means dried out, as washing is.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampers for soiled clothing hold the dirty washing until it is cleaned.

clue.text: Shark on track to find school of small fry

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the nurse shark is a kind of shark
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A shark swims along a set route looking for a shoal of little fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Small fry are young children as well as young fish, and school means a teaching place.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where very young children are taught before primary age is a preschool for little ones.

clue.text: What will eat idly with no limits? Pigs do

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so the pigs hold the kept letters

parts.note: swine are pigs

indicators.note: having no limits means the outer letters are dropped and only the middle is kept

parts.note: the inside of idly

explanation.surface: A question about who eats lazily, answered: pigs do.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word, read as a verb, is the definition, not part of the reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is informal for cheating them out of money by deception.

clue.text: World of expense, the majority suffering cuts

indicators.note: suffering cuts means being trimmed, so each word loses its last letter

parts.note: an expense is a cost
the majority is most

explanation.surface: Across a world of expense, most people are suffering from spending cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe seen as an ordered whole is a synonym for the world in its widest sense.

clue.text: Watch first act of play next to old boy

indicators.note: next to means placed beside, so the two pieces join end to end

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
in tennis play begins with a serve

explanation.surface: Watch the opening act of a play, sitting next to an old schoolmate.
explanation.walkthrough: Play looks theatrical, but the first act is in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something attentively and take notice of it is the verb meaning watch.

clue.text: Light soups, occasionally with a roll, healthy food

indicators.note: a roll turns something over, so the kept letters are read backwards
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Light soups now and then, with a bread roll, make a healthy meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Light looks like an adjective for the soups but is part of the letter source.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese vinegared rice with raw fish and vegetables is widely regarded as nutritious, low-fat eating.

clue.text: One attempting to run over 1000 miles to get more fit

indicators.note: running over something covers it from end to end, so it ends up inside

parts.note: a trier is one who tries
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
m is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A runner attempts a thousand-mile run to get fitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slimmer and in better shape is a comparative of trim, meaning lean and in good condition.

clue.text: High-handed staff with US A&E that's facing raging flu

parts.note: a mast is a staff or pole

indicators.note: something raging is wild and out of control, so the letters go into disorder

parts.note: in the US the emergency room, ER, matches the British accident and emergency department
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An overbearing hospital staff in an American emergency room confront a raging flu outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital casualty department.
explanation.definitionFit: A domineering person imposes their will on others, overbearing and imperious in manner.

clue.text: Briefly fiddle about in board game?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Strad is the short form of Stradivarius, a famous violin

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles briefly with the pieces during a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this game is played at a board on a pub wall rather than on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Players throw pointed missiles at a circular target hung on the wall, often in pubs.

clue.text: Most of its vehicles are big or small in length

definitions.text: Most of its vehicles are big

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
in, as in fashionable, is hip
a yard is a unit of length

explanation.surface: Most of the vehicles are either big or small in length.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of reads like a trimming instruction but belongs to the definition; the vessels built there are mostly large.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where vessels are built and repaired has huge ships as its typical 'vehicles'.

clue.text: Sign of cat eating small creature that sits beside house?

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so the creature goes within the sign

parts.note: Leo, the lion, is the zodiac sign of a big cat
an ant is a small insect

explanation.surface: A cat shows signs of eating a small creature that sits beside the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat by the house looks like a pet, but the cat is the lion of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple shed whose roof rests against an outside wall is built alongside a building.
